picks.title: Interventions for adhesive capsulitis: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

sections.objective: To compare the benefits and harms of therapeutic interventions for adhesive capsulitis.
sections.methods: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
sections.results: A total of 189 randomised controlled trials involving 12 988 participants and 59 interventions were included. Most trials contributing to principal outcomes were at high risk of bias (71% for pain, 72% for function, and 71% for range of motion). At short term follow-up, moderate certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy probably reduced pain compared with usual care (mean difference -1.97 on a 0-10 scale, 95% confidence interval (CI) -2.97 to -0.97). Low certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy may improve function (mean difference -11.42 on a 0-100 scale, 95% CI -16.68 to -6.15), although direct and indirect estimates were limited by important incoherence. For short term range of motion, moderate certainty evidence suggested that manipulation under anaesthesia combined with intra-articular steroid injections probably improved flexion (mean difference 33.29°, 95% CI 11.19° to 55.39°), as did manipulation under anaesthesia alone (26.16°, 8.19° to 44.13°). Low certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy may improve flexion (22.42°, 12.99° to 31.84°) and abduction (18.62°, 8.09° to 29.14°), but both comparisons were limited by important incoherence. At mid-term follow-up, evidence for possible improvements in function with extracorporeal shockwave therapy and flexion with passive mobilisation was of low certainty, while evidence for pain reduction with extracorporeal shockwave therapy was of very low certainty. Most other comparative estimates were supported by low or very low certainty evidence. Comparative safety remained highly uncertain because adverse events were incompletely and inconsistently reported; the absence of reported adverse events should not be interpreted as evidence of absence of harm.
sections.conclusion: Moderate certainty evidence suggests short term pain reduction with extracorporeal shockwave therapy and improved short term flexion with manipulation under anaesthesia, with or without intra-articular steroid injections. Most other treatment effects remain uncertain because of low certainty and incoherence, and comparative safety and mid-term effects are poorly established. The available evidence is mainly short term and outcome specific. Longer term comparative effectiveness, overall benefits and harms, and applicability beyond predominantly primary adhesive capsulitis remain uncertain.
sections.other: Medline, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to 1 May 2025, with an update in November 2025. Randomised controlled trials enrolling adults with adhesive capsulitis, comparing active treatment with another intervention, placebo, or usual care. Pain, function, range of motion, and adverse events. PROSPERO CRD420251070468.

picks.title: Perioperative respiratory adverse events in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy with laryngeal mask airway versus endotracheal tube ventilation: multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To assess the effect of ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA) compared with endotracheal tube (ETT) on perioperative respiratory adverse events (PRAEs) in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
sections.methods: Multicentre, randomised, parallel group trial. 400 children aged ≥2 years and <7 years who were scheduled for adenotonsillectomy under general anaesthesia. Participants were randomised 1:1 to receive ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (n=200) or an endotracheal tube (n=200) during adenotonsillectomy.
sections.results: 400 children (mean age 4.7 (standard deviation 1.0) years; 155 (38.7%) girls) were enrolled between 24 May 2023 and 4 April 2024, with last follow-up on 4 May 2024. LMA was converted to ETT in three participants. Overall, 22.5% (45/200) participants in the LMA group experienced PRAEs versus 57.5% (115/200) in the ETT group (absolute risk difference -35.0 percentage points, 95% confidence interval -43.5 to -25.7; P<0.001). The LMA group had fewer PRAEs in both the intraoperative (9.0% (18/200) v 17.5% (35/200); -8.5, -15.2 to -1.8; P=0.01) and the postoperative period (16.5% (33/200) v 49.5% (99/200); -33.0, -41.2 to -24.0; P<0.001). The LMA group also had a lower proportion of participants with laryngospasm (0.0% v 3.0%; P=0.03), desaturation (15.0% v 28.0%; P=0.002), airway obstruction (3.5% v 12.5%; P<0.001), and severe cough (10.5% v 42.0%; P<0.001). Neither group experienced serious adverse events.
sections.conclusion: Ventilation with an LMA by experienced anaesthesiologists resulted in fewer perioperative respiratory adverse events than ventilation with an ETT in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
sections.other: Four tertiary hospitals in China, 2023-24. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants who developed any perioperative respiratory adverse event (PRAE): laryngospasm, bronchospasm, desaturation, airway obstruction, severe cough, or stridor in the intention-to-treat population.

picks.title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering.
picks.abstract: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease1. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model2,3. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor-encapsulated within a GalNAc-lipid nanoparticle-leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

picks.title: Quantum gases below 10 picokelvin in space.
picks.abstract: Ultracold atom platforms enable low temperatures and long free evolution times, which are crucial for fundamental physics tests and atom interferometry. The lowest equivalent temperature reported in such a system is 38 pK with a free expansion time of 2 s, achieved in atom-chip-based magnetic traps in microgravity. Optical dipole trap (ODT) systems offer better optical access and the flexibility to condense both magnetic and non-magnetic atoms, but have not been used to prepare quantum degenerate gases under microgravity conditions. Here we report an ODT-based Bose-Einstein condensate created aboard the China Space Station, containing 2.0 × 104 atoms, reaching an equivalent temperature of [Formula: see text] pK with a free expansion time of 7.0 s. This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of ODT-based experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space.

picks.title: An information-theoretic framework for inferring T cell dynamics from single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing.
picks.abstract: Single-cell T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing enables simultaneous profiling of gene expression and TCR sequences, providing a coregistered measure of T cell phenotypic diversity and clonal dynamics. However, principled probabilistic frameworks for joint modeling of clonotype and phenotype have remained limited. Here we introduce TCRi, a hierarchical Bayesian information-theoretic framework that infers the joint probability distribution between genetic clonotype and transcriptional phenotype from paired single-cell transcriptomic and TCR sequencing data. TCRi treats phenotype assignment as a probabilistic inference problem: a variational autoencoder embeds single-cell expression into a structured latent space, and a hierarchical Bayesian model learns clonotype-specific phenotype distributions through principled information-sharing across clonotypes, patients and covariates. From these distributions, TCRi computes information-theoretic quantities: clonotypic entropy, phenotypic entropy, phenotypic flux and mutual information between clonotype and phenotype. When TCRi was applied to four real-world datasets comprising 167,118 CD8 T cells from patients with cancer treated with anti-PD-(L)1 immune checkpoint blockade, mutual information emerged as a robust discriminator of therapeutic response.

picks.title: Preparing for responsive management versus renal dialysis in older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity in the UK (Prepare for Kidney Care): a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: The comparative effectiveness of conservative kidney management and dialysis in older people (aged ≥80 years regardless of frailty and comorbidity or aged 65-79 years if frailty or multimorbidity are present) living with kidney failure is unknown. We aimed to assess the relative effectiveness of preparing for responsive management-a protocolised version of conservative kidney management-and preparing for renal dialysis.
sections.methods: Prepare for Kidney Care was a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial conducted in 31 kidney centres in England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. Eligible patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 15 mL/min per 1·73 m2, confirmed by at least one additional reading in the 12 months preceding consent that was not due to acute kidney injury, and were either aged 80 years or older, or aged 65-79 years with a WHO performance status of at least 3 or a Davies comorbidity score of at least 2. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to prepare for responsive management-a patient-centred approach focused on slowing disease progression, active symptom management, and preserving quality of life without the use of dialysis or kidney transplantation-or to prepare for renal dialysis. Randomisation was stratified by centre and minimised by age; a centralised system ensured allocation concealment until randomisation had taken place. The primary outcome was the mean difference in quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), combining length and health-related quality of life from the patient-reported EQ-5D-5L scale, including all follow-up from randomisation to Aug 31, 2025. The primary outcome was analysed by intention to treat in the full analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants, with missing EQ-5D-5L values for living participants imputed. Harms (hospital admissions and dialysis access complications) and adverse events (deaths and hospital admissions, by cause) were assessed in the full analysis set. The trial was registered with ISRCTN, 17133653 (completed).
sections.results: From July 1, 2017, to Aug 31, 2024, 6120 patients were screened across 31 kidney centres in the UK, 445 (7%) of whom were eligible and agreed to be randomly assigned. 228 (51%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for responsive management and 217 (49%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for renal dialysis. Median age was 82 years (IQR 80 to 86) and 137 (31%) of 445 participants were female. After a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years (SD 2·1), mean QALYs were 1·354 (95% CI 1·201 to 1·508) in the prepare for responsive management group and 1·472 (1·288 to 1·655) in the prepare for renal dialysis group (adjusted mean difference -0·147 [95% CI -0·350 to 0·056] p=0·16). Specific harms outcomes were not prespecified, but hospital admission rates were similar in the two groups and dialysis access complications were significantly lower in the prepare for responsive management group (adjusted incident rate ratio 0·41 [95% CI 0·19 to 0·88]), based on 74 events in 36 participants across both groups. There were 667 serious adverse events in the prepare for responsive management group (157 [69%] of 228 participants died, with 510 hospital admissions) and 578 in the prepare for renal dialysis group (136 [63%] of 217 participants died, with 442 hospital admissions). None of these serious adverse events met the criteria for expedited reporting.
sections.conclusion: Among older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity, we found no evidence that either preparing for responsive management or preparing for renal dialysis was superior in terms of QALYs over a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years. This trial provides novel comparative information for clinical decision making.

picks.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.

sections.objective: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis.
sections.methods: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing.
sections.results: At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

picks.title: CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element.
picks.abstract: Noncoding sequences comprise most of the human genome; however, their functional significance remains largely elusive. Using CRISPR tiling mutagenesis with near-PAMless, high-fidelity SpRY-Cas9, we mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene, the 10-kb MYC locus, at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. Essential noncoding base pairs are under strong constraint in the human population but show limited evolutionary conservation across species. Within this landscape, we identified an ultraconserved noncoding RNA element in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) that promotes perinuclear localization of MYC mRNA and nuclear localization of MYC protein through interaction with hnRNP L. Steric-blocking antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting this element selectively eliminate diverse MYC-dependent cancer cells and inhibit growth of patient-derived tumor organoids. Together, these findings establish noncoding sequences as major carriers of functional genetic information and identify a therapeutically actionable RNA element whose targeting disrupts MYC-driven cancer.

items.title: Safety and efficacy of the 0/1 h pathway for myocardial infarction in the emergency department: an international, pragmatic, stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.

sections.objective: The evaluation of patients with suspected myocardial infarction relies on serial measurements of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin. We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of implementing the guideline-recommended 0/1 h pathway, compared with a 0/3 h pathway, in hospitals that had not yet adopted the newer strategy.
sections.methods: PRESC1SE-MI was an international, pragmatic, stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised, controlled, masked-endpoint trial at 19 hospitals in ten countries. The study included consecutive adults presenting to the emergency department with acute non-traumatic chest discomfort and suspected myocardial infarction. Hospitals using a 0/3 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h) as standard care were randomly allocated to implement the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) after 6 months (early implementation) or 12 months (late implementation). The trial was designed to test the non-inferiority of the 0/1 h pathway for safety and its superiority for efficacy. The non-inferiority margin was set at an odds ratio of 1·3. Analyses were done in the full analysis set. The coprimary safety outcome was a composite of death from any cause or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, and the coprimary efficacy outcome was emergency department length of stay. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05649384, and is active but no longer enrolling.
sections.results: Between Dec 1, 2020, and Dec 31, 2024, 71 983 consecutive patient presentations were screened, of which 67 624 (93·9%) met the eligibility criteria and comprised the full analysis set. Median age was 59 years (IQR 46-73); 29 954 (44·3%) patient presentations were in female patients and 37 670 (55·7%) were in male patients. 13 753 (22·2%) of 62 060 patient presentations with available data were in patients with known coronary artery disease, and 5855 (8·7%) patient presentations had an adjudicated index diagnosis of myocardial infarction. Overall, 36 464 patient presentations were managed with a 0/3 h pathway and 31 160 with the 0/1 h pathway. Death from any cause or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 454 (1·2%) patient presentations in the 0/3 h group and in 341 (1·1%) patient presentations in the 0/1 h group (adjusted odds ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·77-1·13]; pnon-inferiority=0·0004). The median emergency department length of stay was 309 min (IQR 203-470) in the 0/3 h pathway and 309 min (207-474) in the 0/1 h pathway (ratio of adjusted median times 1·00 [95% CI 0·97-1·02]; two-sided p=0·65).
sections.conclusion: Implementation of the 0/1 h pathway met the prespecified non-inferiority criterion for the 30-day composite safety outcome but did not shorten emergency department length of stay compared with the 0/3 h pathway. In this setting, implementation of the 0/1 h pathway alone should therefore not be expected to improve emergency department throughput.

items.title: Generalised eruptive histiocytosis mimicking lymphoma relapse in a patient with previous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
items.abstract: A 92-year-old man with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma treated with chemoradiotherapy, and later with radiotherapy for an isolated cutaneous relapse with complete response, presented with a 1-month history of multiple asymptomatic erythematous-to-violaceous papules and nodules on the face, trunk, and upper limbs. Given his oncological history and previous skin involvement, lymphoma relapse was the leading diagnostic concern, with cutaneous metastases and sarcoidosis also considered. However, skin biopsies showed a non-Langerhans cell histiocytic infiltrate expressing CD45, CD68, and CD163, without CD1a, CD20, PAX5, S100, or Langerin expression. Skin and blood flow cytometry identified no abnormal cell populations, and a PET-CT scan showed no abnormal metabolic activity. Clinicopathological correlation narrowed the differential to group C (cutaneous) histiocytosis, and subsequent spontaneous regression of the lesions over 3 months without treatment supported the diagnosis of generalised eruptive histiocytosis. At 15 months of follow-up, there was no recurrence or evidence of active disease. This case illustrates that cutaneous histiocytoses can mimic several inflammatory and neoplastic conditions, including lymphoma relapse, reinforcing the need to actively resist cognitive bias in people who have had cancer through reflective reassessment, broad differential diagnosis, and biopsy confirmation.

items.title: Single-port Robotic Retroperitoneal Nephroureterectomy with Lower Anterior Access: Surgical Technique, Perioperative and Early Oncological Outcomes from a Multi-institutional Series.

sections.objective: To describe lower anterior access single-port robotic radical nephroureterectomy (LAA-SP RNU), including bladder cuff excision (BCE) and lymph node dissection (LND), without repositioning or redocking.
sections.methods: We present a multicenter retrospective series of 47 patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma who underwent LAA-SP RNU at five referral centers (May 2024-July 2025). A single 4-cm extraperitoneal incision enabled nephroureterectomy, BCE, and selective hilar/pelvic LND without repositioning or redocking. Data were evaluated using descriptive analyses, and pentafecta achievement for the full cohort was estimated through Kaplan-Meier analysis.
sections.conclusion: LAA-SP RNU appears feasible and associated with acceptable perioperative and early oncological outcomes in experienced centers. Comparative prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed to establish oncological durability, patient benefit, and cost-effectiveness.
sections.other: Median age of the patients was 72 yr; 95% had high-risk disease. LND was performed in 20 patients (43%). Median docking and operative times were 20 and 220 min, respectively; one procedure was converted to open surgery. Grade ≥3 complications occurred in three patients (6%); median hospital stay was 5 d. Pathology showed pT2 and pT3 disease in 15% and 36%, respectively. At median follow-up of 12.3 mo, seven patients (14.9%) experienced recurrence, including five intravesical recurrences; two died from metastatic disease. The 12-mo Kaplan-Meier estimate of pentafecta achievement was 76.7% (95% confidence interval, 62.8-90.5%). This study is limited by potential referral-center and patient-selection bias, heterogeneity in LND and postoperative management, limited follow-up, and the absence of cost-effectiveness data.

items.title: A 3D Deep Learning Model for Assessing Concomitant Pulmonary Embolism Risk by Integrating Clinical and Computed Tomography Venography Features in Patients with Lower Extremity Deep Venous Thrombosis.

sections.objective: The aim of this study was to develop and validate a multimodal deep learning (DL) model integrating clinical and computed tomography venography (CTV) features for predicting concomitant acute pulmonary embolism (PE) risk in patients with lower extremity deep venous thrombosis (LEDVT).
sections.methods: This multicentre retrospective study enrolled patients with LEDVT undergoing both computed tomography pulmonary angiography and lower extremity CTV. Centre 1 data were used for model training and internal validation, while data from centres 2 and 3 were used for external testing. Clinical models (logistic regression [LR], random forest [RF], support vector machine [SVM], and XGBoost), 3D DL models (VGG-11, VGG-16, ResNet-18, Res2Net-50, and DenseNet-121), and combined models (LR, RF, SVM, and XGBoost) integrating clinical, imaging, and DL features were developed to select the best performer, which was further benchmarked against validated clinical risk scores (Wells score and modified Geneva score).
sections.results: A total of 348 patients from centre 1 were randomly split into training and internal validation sets, and 127 patients from two independent institutions formed the external testing cohort. The optimal LR clinical, 3D VGG-16 DL, and SVM combined models achieved external testing area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.776, 0.789, and 0.836, respectively. DeLong tests confirmed that the SVM combined model significantly outperformed the LR clinical model and validated clinical scores (all p < .050) on the external testing set, while yielding a comparable AUC to the 3D VGG-16 DL model. Decision curve analysis indicated higher net benefit for the SVM combined model, alongside superior calibration, and positive net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement values.
sections.conclusion: The SVM combined model integrating clinical, imaging, and DL features demonstrated robust performance, offering a promising tool for predicting concomitant acute PE in patients with LEDVT.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ulinastatin in the Treatment of Patients with Sepsis: The ADJUST Trial.

sections.objective: Urinary trypsin inhibitor (ulinastatin, UTI) has shown potential survival benefits in sepsis; however, conclusive clinical evidence is lacking.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adult ICU patients with sepsis meeting Sepsis-3 criteria within 48 hours of admission were randomized (1:1) to receive intravenous UTI (400,000 IU every 8 hours) or placebo, for up to 10 days in addition to standard care. Randomization was stratified by site and septic shock. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included ICU, hospital, and 90-day mortality, and ICU/hospital length of stay.
sections.results: Of 347 patients randomized, 340 (169 UTI, 171 placebo) received intervention and were included in the safety analysis; after 5 post-intervention withdrawals, 335 (165 UTI, 170 placebo) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. At 28 days, death had occurred in 39 of 165 patients (23.6%) in the UTI group and in 39 of 170 patients (22.9%) in the placebo group (absolute difference, 0.7% [95% CI -8.4% to 9.7%]; P = .98; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.61, P = .90). Secondary outcomes were similar in the two groups. Adverse events occurred in 56.8% (96/169) of UTI and 42.7% (73/171) of placebo patients (absolute difference 14.1%, 95% CI 3.6%-24.6%; P = 0.009).
sections.conclusion: In patients with sepsis, adjunctive UTI did not reduce mortality compared with placebo. Routine use of UTI for sepsis is not supported by these findings.
sections.other: In patients with sepsis, does adjunctive ulinastatin, compared with placebo, reduce 28-day all-cause mortality?

items.title: Eyelid injury and associations with visual outcomes and globe removal after open globe injury: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Eyelid injury is identifiable at presentation, but its relationship with visual prognosis and globe survival has not been systematically synthesized. This prospectively registered systematic review and meta-analysis (CRD420261441414) evaluated the association between eyelid injury and visual or globe survival outcomes among patients with open globe injury (OGI).MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through February 21, 2026. Studies reporting visual acuity (VA) or globe survival outcomes stratified by eyelid injury status were included. Eyelid injury encompassed eyelid laceration, lid involvement, eyelid wound, or traumatic involvement as reported by study authors. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E, and certainty using GRADE. Random-effects models generated pooled odds ratios (ORs), with heterogeneity quantified using I². Twenty-one observational studies were included; 14 contributed to quantitative synthesis. Eyelid injury was associated with higher odds of VA worse than 20/200 (OR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.20-2.50; p=0.0036; I²=0.0%), hand motion or worse (OR, 4.99; 95% CI, 2.04-12.21; p=0.0004; I²=49.7%), no light perception or worse (OR, 3.04; 95% CI, 2.05-4.51; p<0.0001; I²=0.0%), and globe removal (OR, 4.22; 95% CI, 1.73-10.34; p=0.0016; I²=53.0%). The association with VA worse than 20/400 was directionally similar but not significant (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.81-1.87; p=0.3362; I²=0.0%). Low to very-low certainty evidence suggests that eyelid injury is associated with worse visual outcomes and increased odds of globe removal after OGI. Because the pooled estimates are based on crude, unadjusted comparisons, eyelid injury may reflect established markers of injury severity rather than provide independent prognostic information.

items.title: Left Subclavian Artery Revascularization and Early Neurological Outcomes After Zone 2 TEVAR.

sections.objective: LSA revascularization is generally favored when intentional LSA coverage is planned during elective zone 2 TEVAR, whereas in urgent settings the decision is individualized according to anatomy, ischemic risk, and clinical urgency. This study evaluated the association between preoperative or concomitant LSA revascularization and early neurological outcomes after zone 2 TEVAR.
sections.methods: This single-center retrospective study included 32 patients who underwent zone 2 TEVAR with intentional LSA coverage between January 2018 and December 2024. Patients were classified according to whether LSA revascularization was performed before or concomitantly with TEVAR (Rev+, n=21) or not (Rev-, n=11). The primary endpoint was any 30 day neurological complication, including ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), and spinal cord ischemia (SCI). Major neurological events, defined as stroke or SCI, were additionally evaluated.
sections.results: Early neurological complications occurred in 4/21 patients (19.0%) in the Rev+ group and 3/11 (27.3%) in the Rev- group (p=.667), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of -8.2 percentage points (95% CI, -39.4 to 23.0) and a risk ratio of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.19-2.58). Major neurological events occurred in 3/21 (14.3%) and 2/11 (18.2%) patients, respectively (p=1.000). Stroke occurred in 3/21 (14.3%) Rev+ patients and 1/11 (9.1%) Rev- patients, while SCI occurred in no Rev+ patients and in 1/11 (9.1%) Rev- patients. LSA revascularization was not significantly associated with the primary endpoint (OR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.12-3.34; p=.582). Results remained similar after separate adjustment for age, dissection, urgency, coronary artery disease, and chronic kidney disease. Sensitivity analyses using major neurological events as the endpoint and including postoperative LSA revascularization in the exposure definition also yielded similar results.
sections.conclusion: Preoperative or concomitant LSA revascularization during zone 2 TEVAR was associated with a numerically lower rate of early neurological complications, although the difference was not statistically significant. Larger studies are needed to better define the association between LSA revascularization and neurological outcomes after zone 2 TEVAR.

items.title: VOLUME ADJUSTED CALCIUM ANALYSIS OF AORTOILIAC ATHEROSCLEROSIS AS A PREDICTOR OF AMPUTATION FREE SURVIVAL.

sections.objective: Pre-operative cross-sectional imaging guides surgical planning in vascular surgery. Despite the relationship between atherosclerotic burden and surgical success, no studies have adjusted atherosclerotic burden according to lumen volume. Given variability in vessel diameter and significance of aortoiliac disease, we developed a volume-adjusted calcium score (VACS) and evaluated its association with patient outcomes.
sections.methods: This single-institution retrospective study included 187 patients over nine years who underwent peripheral vascular intervention. Using TeraRecon, calcium and patent lumen volumes were quantified along a contiguous aorto-iliac segment totaling 10 cm generating a VACS. An intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) assessed inter-rater reliability. Patients were stratified into two groups. Primary outcomes were death at one year and amputation-free survival. Secondary outcomes were re-interventions and number of arteries treated.
sections.results: Intervention type did not differ between the two groups. Patients with higher VACS were more likely older, have CHF, COPD, or hypertension. Patient in the higher VACS group had greater number of arteries treated, subsequent vascular interventions, and one-year all-cause mortality. A Cox-regression model demonstrated a VACSgreater than 0.33 was independently associated with decreased amputation-free survival at one year (HR 2.24, p=0.019).
sections.conclusion: In patients undergoing intervention for aortoiliac occlusive disease, higher VACS was independently associated with worse one-year amputation free survival. Incorporating patent lumen volume into VACS appears to capture a systemic atherosclerotic burden not fully reflected by traditional lesion-specific assessments.

items.title: Prevalence of concomitant aneurysms in patients with thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms who underwent Fenestrated/Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair (F-BEVAR).

sections.objective: To determine the prevalence of synchronous ascending aortic and peripheral arterial aneurysms in patients with Crawford extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA) undergoing fenestrated/branched endovascular aneurysm repair (F/BEVAR).
sections.methods: We performed a single-center retrospective review of prospectively collected data from patients with Crawford extent I-IV TAAA treated with F/BEVAR under a physician-sponsored investigational device exemption. The preoperative CTA obtained for device planning was used to measure the ascending aorta and bilateral common iliac (CIA), hypogastric (HA), and common femoral (CFA) arteries using centerline reconstruction. Bilateral popliteal artery (PA) diameters were obtained from preoperative arterial duplex imaging. An aneurysm was defined as a vessel diameter >50% greater than the expected normal diameter for that arterial bed, using references available from literature. Multivariable logistic regression included sex, obesity, race/ethnicity, TAAA diameter ≥7 cm, and prior aortic dissection. A sensitivity analysis was performed after excluding patients with prior aortic dissection.
sections.results: Among 249 patients (mean age, 70.8±8.6 years; 40.2% women), 177 (71.1%) had at least one concomitant aneurysm. Race/ethnicity was 75.1% NH-White, 21.7% NH-Black, 0.8% Hispanic, and 2.4% Other. Among evaluable patients, aneurysm prevalence was 12.0% in the ascending aorta (29/242), 62.8% in the CIA (140/223), 42.1% in the HA (98/233), 22.2% in the PA (51/230), and 9.6% in the CFA (22/228). On multivariable analysis, CIA aneurysm was associated with obesity, non-White race/ethnicity, and TAAA diameter ≥7 cm; HA aneurysm with male sex, obesity, and prior dissection; CFA aneurysm with male sex; PA aneurysm with male sex and prior dissection; and ascending aortic aneurysm with TAAA diameter ≥7 cm and prior dissection. After exclusion of 46 patients with prior dissection, concomitant aneurysms remained a common occurrence.
sections.conclusion: Concomitant aneurysms are common in patients undergoing F/BEVAR for Crawford extent I-IV TAAA. Several associations remained significant after multivariable adjustment. These findings should be interpreted in the context of a single-center referral population, variable arterial-bed denominators, possible diffuse arteriomegaly, and residual confounding. The prevalence of PA aneurysm supports further evaluation of selective popliteal assessment; however, this study does not support a universal screening recommendation or establish an effect on management, outcomes, or cost.

items.title: Posterior Transverse Plication of Tortuous Internal Carotid Arteries During Carotid Endarterectomy.

sections.objective: Excessive tortuosity of the internal carotid artery (ICA) can create a risk of kinking after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) with patch angioplasty. Posterior transverse plication (PTP) shortens and straightens the ICA without arterial transection or resection. This study reviewed our outcomes with PTP followed by patch angioplasty during CEA.
sections.methods: A retrospective cohort study identified patients who underwent CEA between 2006 and 2023. Patients treated with PTP and patch angioplasty (PTP+P) were compared with a contemporaneous cohort undergoing CEA with Dacron patch closure alone (DP) for the same atherosclerotic carotid disease. Early and long-term outcomes included neurologic events, restenosis, pseudoaneurysm formation, reintervention, and survival.
sections.results: Of 168 carotid interventions, 116 met inclusion criteria: 16 PTP+P and 100 DP. Patients in the PTP+P cohort were older and had higher rates of chronic renal insufficiency and coronary artery disease. There was no 30-day mortality or postoperative TIA/stroke in either cohort. During follow-up, no ipsilateral ischemic neurologic event occurred, and there was no significant difference in restenosis, pseudoaneurysm formation, reintervention, or overall survival. In adjusted analysis, increasing age was associated with worse survival, while PTP was not.
sections.conclusion: In this small series, adding PTP during CEA before patch angioplasty appeared safe for correcting ICA tortuosity. The complication profile was similar to that of patients with straighter ICAs who underwent DP closure alone. A wide patch and intraoperative duplex ultrasound are advisable to prevent and detect technical narrowing at the plication site.
sections.other: Carotid endarterectomy; internal carotid artery tortuosity; posterior transverse plication; patch angioplasty; restenosis.

items.title: Repair durability following fenestrated versus chimney endovascular repair for elective juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms: a multicenter cohort study.

sections.objective: To compare repair durability following elective fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) and chimney endovascular aneurysm repair (ChEVAR) for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms using complementary procedural, imaging, and clinical outcome measures.
sections.methods: A retrospective multicenter cohort study was performed across five high-volume aortic referral centers. Consecutive patients undergoing elective FEVAR or ChEVAR for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms were included. Baseline characteristics, technical success, endoleaks, secondary aortic intervention, aneurysm sac remodeling, and target vessel patency were compared. Repair durability was assessed by integrating proximal seal integrity, longitudinal aneurysm sac remodeling, and freedom from secondary aortic intervention. Continuous variables were compared using Student's t test or the Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using χ2 or Fisher's exact tests. Statistical significance was defined as P < .05.
sections.results: A total of 130 patients underwent elective repair, including 77 treated with FEVAR and 53 with ChEVAR. Baseline demographic characteristics, aneurysm diameter, and duration of follow-up were similar between groups. Technical success was comparable (98.7% vs 98.1%; P = .76), and target vessel patency exceeded 95% in both cohorts (P = .38). Type Ia endoleak occurred less frequently following FEVAR than ChEVAR (1.3% vs 22.6%; P < .001), with a lower incidence of all Type I endoleaks (Types Ia, Ib, and Ic) (7.8% vs 26.4%; P = .006). Secondary aortic intervention was also less common following FEVAR (10.4% vs 30.2%; P = .006). Progressive aneurysm sac regression was observed following FEVAR, with a mean reduction of 11 mm at 24 months, whereas ChEVAR demonstrated limited early regression followed by late sac re-expansion, resulting in an overall 2-mm reduction. Mean aneurysm sac diameter was significantly smaller following FEVAR compared with ChEVAR at both 12 months (55 vs 59 mm; P = .01) and 24 months (51 vs 63 mm; P < .001).
sections.conclusion: Elective FEVAR and ChEVAR achieved similarly high technical success and target vessel patency for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms. During mid-term follow-up, FEVAR was associated with lower rates of proximal attachment-site failure, greater aneurysm sac regression, and fewer secondary aortic interventions. These concordant procedural, imaging, and clinical outcomes suggest that integrated longitudinal assessment provides a more comprehensive evaluation of repair durability following complex endovascular aneurysm repair than technical success alone.

items.title: Risk Prediction With a Type Ia-Oriented Proximal Neck Anatomic Severity Grading Score After EVAR.

sections.objective: We developed an exploratory Type Ia-oriented proximal neck Anatomic Severity Grading Score (Type Ia-ASGS) and assessed its association with postoperative type Ia endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR).
sections.methods: We analyzed 304 elective standard EVAR patients treated during 2016-April 2024 with an Ankura endograft (Lifetech). Neck measurements were proximal diameter (A), distal diameter (B), and centerline length (C). The score assigned 1 point each for C ≤15 mm, max(A, B) >28 mm, and B - A ≥3 mm, and 2 points each for angulation >60° and calcification. The theoretical range was 0-7; weights reflected observed univariable associations.
sections.results: Mean clinical and imaging follow-up was 27.6 ± 3.2 months, with final follow-up in June 2026. Type Ia endoleak occurred in 14/304 patients (4.6%). Observed event proportions were 1.2%, 2.8%, and 28.1% in exploratory low (0-1), intermediate (2-3), and high (≥4) score categories (p < 0.001). Each point was associated with greater odds of type Ia endoleak (odds ratio, 2.78; 95% confidence interval, 1.80-4.29). Apparent area under the curve was 0.859 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 0.750-0.943). Individual event and censoring dates were unavailable for time-to-event analysis.
sections.conclusion: The Type Ia-ASGS was associated with postoperative type Ia endoleak in this derivation cohort. Its heuristic weights and exploratory categories require independent validation before clinical use.

items.title: Successful Management of Infective Native Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Associated With Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis in a 77-year-Old Man.
items.abstract: BackgroundInfected native abdominal aortic aneurysm (INAAA) is a rare but life-threatening condition characterized by rapid progression and high mortality.Case SummaryWe report a 77-year-old male with a history of arterial hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and stage IVB hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma, presenting with lumbar pain and mild inflammatory activation, including leukocytes 8.8 ×10³/µL and C-reactive protein 3.6 mg/dL (normal <0.50 mg/dL). Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 50-mm infrarenal aneurysm, with periaortic inflammatory changes and a periaortic hematoma. A multidisciplinary decision, made 3 hours after admission, favored urgent open surgical repair with resection and in situ reconstruction. Midline laparotomy with debridement and resection of the affected aorta was performed; in situ reconstruction was carried out using a rifampicin soaked bifurcated Dacron graft covered with bovine pericardium with anastomoses to healthy aortic and iliac segments. Intraoperative cultures identified Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis, rare pathogens in this context. Targeted therapy included intravenous ceftriaxone during hospitalization, followed by oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and doxycycline for seven weeks. Histopathology confirmed chronic granulomatous abscessed inflammation. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged home on postoperative day 17. At six months, follow-up imaging demonstrated a patent reconstruction without signs of persistent infection.ConclusionThese findings highlight the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and coordinated multidisciplinary management in achieving optimal outcomes in INAAA, particularly when atypical microorganisms complicate diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making.

items.title: Preserved Choroidal Thickness and Vascularity Index in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Report No. 2 from the ORNET Study.
items.abstract: In this prospective ORNET analysis, obstructive sleep apnea was not associated with significant changes in choroidal thickness or vascularity index as measured by optical coherence tomography, suggesting relative preservation of choroidal tissue.

items.title: Community health worker-led home blood pressure monitoring in rural sub-Saharan Africa: a diagnostic accuracy study.

sections.objective: Home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) coordinated by community health workers (CHWs) is a potential strategy to improve hypertension detection in sub-Saharan Africa, yet data on its diagnostic performance in this setting are scarce. We aimed to determine the diagnostic accuracy of CHW-coordinated HBPM in Kenya and The Gambia using daytime ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) as the reference standard.
sections.methods: In this cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study, we recruited a random sample of representative age-stratified individuals aged 30 years or older from the general population of two health and demographic surveillance systems in Kilifi, Kenya, and Kiang West, The Gambia. We used the latest enumeration lists of the two health and demographic surveillance systems as sampling frames and performed computer-generated random sampling within five predefined age strata (30-39 years, 40-49 years, 50-59 years, 60-69 years, and ≥70 years). Pregnant women were excluded, and participants were eligible to participate irrespective of previous hypertension status. CHWs trained and provided participants with HBPM devices for self-measurement of blood pressure twice a day, for a minimum of 3 days and a maximum of 7 days. For the reference standard measurement, an ABPM device was fitted by CHWs, and ambulatory blood pressure was measured every 15 min during the day and 30 min at night. We used blood pressure cutoffs derived from the European Society of Hypertension to determine the age-standardised measures of accuracy (sensitivities, specificities, positive predictive values [PPVs] and negative predictive values [NPVs], positive likelihood ratios [LR+] and negative likelihood ratios [LR-] and area under receiver operating characteristic curves) of HBPM among participants who had valid HBPM and ABPM measurements.
sections.results: Between Aug 18, 2023, and Dec 13, 2024, from 1452 eligible participants, we included 1279 participants with valid HBPM and ABPM measurements (696 in Kenya and 583 in The Gambia). In 1279 participants, the median age was 54 years (IQR 43-66), 805 (62·9%) were women, and 474 (37·1%) were men. The age-standardised prevalence of hypertension on daytime ABPM was 23·1% (95% CI 19·9-26·2) in Kenya and 27·1% (23·6-30·6) in The Gambia while the respective prevalences on HBPM were 32·5% (29·1-35·8) and 31·2% (27·5-34·9). The age-standardised sensitivities and specificities of HBPM were 82·6% (76·2-89·0) and 82·4% (79·0-85·7) in Kenya and 68·7% (61·3-76·1) and 83·5% (79·7-87·2) in The Gambia. The age-standardised PPVs and NPVs were 58·6% (52·0-65·2) and 94·0% (91·6-96·4) in Kenya and 59·9% (52·5-67·2) and 88·1% (84·8-91·4) in The Gambia, respectively. The age-standardised LR+ and LR- were 4·68 (3·67-5·69) and 0·21 (0·13-0·29) in Kenya and 4·15 (3·09-5·21) and 0·37 (0·28-0·46) in The Gambia, respectively. In both countries, the area under receiver operating characteristic curve for HBPM was above 75%.
sections.conclusion: HBPM showed moderate-to-high sensitivity and high specificity for detecting hypertension in two rural sub-Saharan African communities. HBPM represents a promising alternative for increasing hypertension awareness in rural sub-Saharan Africa.

items.title: Ganaplacide plus lumefantrine solid dispersion formulation for children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria (KALUMI): an open-label, multicentre, randomised, controlled, adaptive, phase 2, non-inferiority trial.

sections.objective: Ganaplacide plus lumefantrine solid dispersion formulation (SDF) is a novel antimalarial combination shown to be effective and well tolerated in adults, adolescents, and children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria. Here, we aimed to assess food effects on drug exposure and non-inferiority of ganaplacide plus lumefantrine SDF to artemether-lumefantrine.
sections.methods: This open-label, multicentre, randomised, controlled, adaptive, phase 2, non-inferiority trial was conducted at ten clinics and hospitals in Burkina Faso, Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, Gabon, and DR Congo. Eligible patients had microscopically confirmed uncomplicated P falciparum malaria. In run-in cohorts 1 and 2, patients (aged 12 years to <18 years with bodyweight ≥35·0 kg) were randomly assigned (1:1) to dosing in the fed group (standard meal 400-500 calories, with 20-30 g of fat) or in the fasted group. Patients received ganaplacide 400 mg plus lumefantrine SDF 240 mg (run-in cohort 1) and ganaplacide 400 mg plus lumefantrine SDF 480 mg (run-in cohort 2) once per day for 2 days. In the main part (cohort 1 [age 2 years to <12 years] and cohort 2 [age 6 months to <2 years]), patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to ganaplacide plus lumefantrine SDF (at the dose regimen selected from run-in cohorts, adjusted by bodyweight) or artemether-lumefantrine for 3 days. Randomisation, using an Interactive response technology system, was stratified by age group and country (cohort 1) or by country (run-in cohorts and cohort 2). Food effects on the bioavailability of ganaplacide and lumefantrine were assessed in run-in cohorts. The primary endpoint for the main part of the study was PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response on day 29 in the per protocol population. The non-inferiority margin was 10%. Safety and tolerability was a secondary endpoint. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04546633 (completed).
sections.results: Between Feb 16, 2021, and July 14, 2024, 577 patients were screened and 282 were ineligible. 51 patients were enrolled in run-in cohort 1, 24 in run-in cohort 2, and 220 in the main part (110 each assigned to ganaplacide plus lumefantrine SDF or artemether-lumefantrine). Two (4%) patients discontinued early in run-in cohort 1 and all 24 in run-in cohort 2 completed the study. Across run-in cohorts 1 and 2, the food effect on ganaplacide was small (mean fed:fasted ratios from 0·98 to 1·41), but a significant food effect was observed for lumefantrine (mean ratios ranging from 1·48 to 2·87). Ganaplacide 400 mg plus lumefantrine SDF 480 mg given once per day for 3 days with a light meal (100-300 calories, with 5-10 g of fat) was selected as the full dose and 206 (94%) of 220 patients completed the main part. For PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response on day 29, response rates were 97 (99% [95% CI 94 to 100]) of 98 in the ganaplacide plus lumefantrine SDF group and 98 (99% [95 to 100]) of 99 in the artemether-lumefantrine group (treatment difference -0·0% [-2·9 to 2·8]), with the lower limit of 95% CI above -10%. The most common adverse events were vomiting (32 [29%] of 110 in the ganaplacide plus lumefantrine SDF group vs 12 [11%] of 110 in the artemether-lumefantrine group) and hypokalaemia (27 [25%] vs 16 [15%]).
sections.conclusion: Ganaplacide 400 mg plus lumefantrine SDF 480 mg once per day for 3 days with a light meal was non-inferior to artemether-lumefantrine for patients with uncomplicated P falciparum malaria. This regimen was further evaluated in a phase 3 trial (NCT05842954).

items.title: Self-amplifying RNA vaccines encoding chimeric and mosaic hemagglutinins confer immunity against phylogenetically diverse influenza A viruses.
items.abstract: Seasonal influenza vaccines require annual reformulation due to antigenic drift and provide suboptimal protection. Here, we evaluate self-amplifying mRNA (samRNA) vaccines encoding chimeric (cHA) and mosaic (mHA) hemagglutinins representing influenza A virus HA phylogenetic groups 1 and 2. Following prime-boost immunization, group 1 cHA vaccines (cH8/1-cH5/1) elicit broad cross-reactive antibodies and confer complete protection against diverse H1N1 strains covering decades of antigenic drift. Group 2 vaccines (cH4/3-cH15/3 and mH10/3-mH14/3) provide comparable breadth against multiple H3N2 strains and heterosubtypic H7N9 challenge, with cHA samRNA showing superior cross-group protection. Protection is associated with Fc-mediated effector functions and CD4+ T cell responses, with minimal hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing titers. Passive serum transfer confirms antibody-mediated protection independent of cellular immunity. Protective immunity is maintained at doses as low as 0.4 μg, demonstrating the dose-sparing advantage of the samRNA platform. These results support samRNA-delivered cHA and mHA antigens as promising candidates for broadly protective influenza vaccines.

items.title: Neural interface instructs layer 4-appropriate circuit reconstruction with engrafted human brain organoids and improves visually guided behavior.
items.abstract: Repairing precise neural microcircuitry after cortical injury remains a pivotal challenge. Human brain organoids (hBOs) are a promising cell source, but disorganized integration limits their therapeutic potential. Here, we demonstrated that targeted neuromodulation, steered by endogenous narrowband gamma (NBG) rhythms, instructed structural and functional integration of hBO grafts in the injured adult mouse visual cortex. Using a neural interface system, we promoted general graft-host coupling and then delivered NBG-rhythmic stimulation to specific functional clusters. This strategy guided the emergence of layer 4-appropriate molecular and functional properties in grafts, enabled bidirectional connectivity with the host visual circuit, and supported the development of advanced visual processing, including direction selectivity in hBO neurons. Electrophysiologically, graft spiking phase locked to host NBG oscillations. Behaviorally, host visual acuity and contrast sensitivity were significantly restored. Our work established a framework for circuit-level repair, highlighting a synergistic strategy that moves beyond cell replacement to direct the assembly of neural grafts.

items.title: Exercise-Induced Tricuspid Regurgitation: Clinical Predictors and Hemodynamic Implications.

sections.objective: Exercise-induced preload/afterload changes could affect tricuspid regurgitation (TR). The study aims to assess exercise-induced TR (exTR+), its consequences, and predictors.
sections.methods: Consecutive patients underwent exercise cardiac catheterization and three-dimensional echocardiography. ExTR+ was defined as a ≥1 grade increase in TR severity.
sections.results: ExTR+ occurred in 34% of 132 patients. Patients with exTR+ were older, had more atrial fibrillation, higher natriuretic peptides/heart failure with preserved ejection fraction probability scores, higher filling pressures, and lower cardiac output (P < 0.05). ExTR+ displayed greater right ventricular dilation, right atrial pressure rise, lower cardiac output, and lower oxygen consumption (P < 0.05). Exercise rather than resting TR regurgitant volume was more associated with cardiac output and oxygen consumption. Baseline TR, atrial fibrillation, and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (OR: 1.065, 4.97, and 1.0004 per pg/mL, respectively, P < 0.05) predicted exTR+ (area under the curve: 0.91).
sections.conclusion: ExTR+ is frequent, identifies heart failure with preserved ejection fraction-like phenotypes with a maladaptive exercise response, and adds information beyond resting TR.

items.title: Age reshapes selection on melanoma driver mutations.
items.abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for melanoma. However, it is unclear whether aging fuels tumor evolution by altering mutation rates, changing the microenvironmentally induced selection on drivers, or both. We analyzed 5472 melanomas, estimating how selection on individual variants changes with patient age while accounting for differing neutral mutation rates. Neutral mutation rates increased only modestly with age; ultraviolet damage remained predominant, but endogenous processes increasingly contributed to older tumors. In contrast, selection on major drivers was strongly age dependent: The advantage of BRAF V600E declined precipitously with age, whereas NRAS Q61 mutations gained advantage. TERT promoter mutations became more frequent, yet less advantageous. Aging therefore reshapes melanoma evolution primarily by altering selection, motivating age-conscious evaluation of clinical biomarkers and therapies.

items.title: Thoracic epidural versus paravertebral blockade for reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain (TOPIC-2): open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of paravertebral blockade versus thoracic epidural during the perioperative period in reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain.
sections.methods: Open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Adult patients undergoing thoracotomy randomised (1:1) to either paravertebral blockade or thoracic epidural using a web based service between January 2019 and September 2023. Participants in the paravertebral group received three single-shot paravertebral injections of local anaesthetic before incision followed by placement of a paravertebral catheter. Participants in the epidural group had a thoracic epidural catheter placed and loaded with local anaesthetic before incision.
sections.results: 770 patients were enrolled, of which 428 (56%) were male (mean (standard deviation, SD) age 66.6 (11.0) years). After 33 exclusions of patients after randomisation who did not proceed to thoracotomy, 737 remained in the modified intention-to-treat population (364 in the paravertebral group, 373 in the epidural group). Six months after randomisation, 59 (22%) of 272 participants in the paravertebral group and 47 (16%) of 292 participants in the epidural group developed chronic post-thoracotomy pain (adjusted risk ratio 1.32 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93 to 1.86), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI -0.01 to 0.11), P=0.12). During the acute phase, worst and average pain was greater on day 1 with paravertebral blockade (adjusted mean difference 7.7 mm (95% CI 2.8 to 12.5 mm) and 7.0 mm (95% CI 2.7 to 11.2 mm), respectively), but no different on days 2-3. Hypotension was less common in the paravertebral group than the epidural group (12% v 18%, respectively, adjusted risk ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.94), adjusted risk difference -0.06 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.01)), as was pruritis (4% v 12%, adjusted risk ratio 0.37 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.64), adjusted risk difference -0.07 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.03)), although more participants in this group experienced urinary retention (12% v 6%, adjusted risk ratio 2.21 (95% CI 1.35 to 3.61), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.09)), complications were similar otherwise.
sections.conclusion: Paravertebral blockade did not reduce chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six month follow-up compared to thoracic epidural. Thoracic epidural provided marginally better acute pain relief one day after the operation, but showed no difference thereafter. Postoperative complications were comparable between groups. The findings support the ongoing use of both techniques.
sections.other: 15 thoracic centres in the UK. The primary outcome was incidence of chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six months after randomisation, defined as a 100 mm visual analogue score greater than or equal to 40 mm (indicating moderate pain) when considering worst chest pain over the past week. Secondary outcomes included acute pain (visual analogue score of 100 mm) and complications.

items.title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch.
items.abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

items.title: Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China.
items.abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level)1, significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

items.title: Eating disorders.
items.abstract: The eating and feeding disorders are serious psychiatric disorders at the mind-body interface, often with an exceptionally high burden for affected individuals, their families and supporters, and wider society. In anorexia nervosa, high acute medical risk and patients' ambivalence about treatment can make a challenging combination that can impede engagement. First-line treatments for eating disorders are mainly psychological, with medications playing an adjunctive role. Novel biological and technology-based interventions are only slowly emerging. Compared with other psychiatric disorders, research into these disorders is seriously underfunded. Many uncertainties regarding their aetiology, maintenance, and treatment remain. Controversies mainly concern the treatment and care of those with the most severe and longstanding forms of illness. Advances in knowledge are most likely to arise from longitudinal studies combining multimodal assessments, using big data to develop better mechanistic understanding, and greater use of flexible trial designs to allow development of more personalised and precise interventions.

items.title: Quantum gases below 10 picokelvin in space.
items.abstract: Ultracold atom platforms enable low temperatures and long free evolution times, which are crucial for fundamental physics tests and atom interferometry. The lowest equivalent temperature reported in such a system is 38 pK with a free expansion time of 2 s, achieved in atom-chip-based magnetic traps in microgravity. Optical dipole trap (ODT) systems offer better optical access and the flexibility to condense both magnetic and non-magnetic atoms, but have not been used to prepare quantum degenerate gases under microgravity conditions. Here we report an ODT-based Bose-Einstein condensate created aboard the China Space Station, containing 2.0 × 104 atoms, reaching an equivalent temperature of [Formula: see text] pK with a free expansion time of 7.0 s. This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of ODT-based experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space.

items.title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake.
items.abstract: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.

items.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition.
items.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

items.abstract: Long-term monitoring reveals how a fault relocks for a future earthquake after a massive rupture.

items.abstract: A computational approach to learning reproduced key features of child language development.
