items.abstract: A new algorithm for protecting privacy can improve the accuracy of population statistics.

items.title: When soil is left undisturbed.
items.abstract: Conservation agriculture reframes farming, risk, and resilience in Africa.

items.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor.
items.abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ. Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli-electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

items.title: Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression.
items.abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

items.title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply.
items.abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades-or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of "abruptness" during DO events.

items.title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening.
items.abstract: Molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, including through ternary complex formation, have been established as key therapeutics. Yet they can be challenging to discover, as standard screening approaches often lack throughput or fail to directly assay multibody interactions. We addressed this by combining DNA nanoswitch-based selection of nucleotide-encoded libraries with next-generation sequencing to create FIND (Functional Interaction-based Nanoswitch Discovery), which enables ultrahigh-throughput discovery of compounds that induce or increase protein-protein interactions. We demonstrate FIND by discovering nanobodies that stabilize the interaction between angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 and the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and by discovering agonists of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma from a DNA-barcoded small-molecule library. By enabling rapid discovery of molecular modulators, FIND could lead to new therapeutics across many conditions.

items.title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
items.abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients' plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolvens, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

items.title: The power of noise.
items.abstract: Noise measurements untangle a decades-old puzzle in high-temperature superconductivity.

items.title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease.
items.abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

items.title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.
items.abstract: Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis-associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell-dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1-positive (ANXA1+) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8+ T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.

items.title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat.
items.abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

items.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists in addiction therapy.
items.abstract: Use of GLP-1-based therapies for addiction could provide a bridge toward whole-person health care.

items.title: In Other Journals.
items.abstract: Editors' selections from the current scientific literature.

items.title: Obesity management medications: The way forward.
items.abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

items.title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems.
items.abstract: Hubbard systems are paradigmatic realizations of strongly correlated many-body systems. Introducing additional species breaks the SU(2) symmetry of the Hubbard model and leads to a wide variety of new exotic quantum phases. Here, we extended quantum gas microscopy to three-flavor Fermi lattice gases in the Hubbard regime. Relying on site- and flavor-resolved detection, we studied the phase diagram of the three-flavor Hubbard model and found signatures of flavor-selective localization and selective pairing at temperatures down to the tunneling energy scale. Our measurements were then compared with numerical linked-cluster expansion calculations. Further increase of phase space density may enable the observation of a distinct pair Mott phase at half filling and shows a path toward the study of color superfluidity and other aspects of quantum chromodynamics.

items.abstract: Highlights from the Science family of journals.

items.title: A cultural history of altered artifacts.
items.abstract: New tools feed humanity's ancient impulse to embellish and self-aggrandize, but future scholars will be prepared.

items.title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children's everyday speech.
items.abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child's natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child's ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child's learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

items.title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling.
items.abstract: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer-enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a "stamping and stacking" (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. Honeycomb-like chips are stamped from nitinol (NiTi) thin sheets and then stacked into a layered tubular structure to increase heat exchange surface and at the same time avoid buckling and splitting failures encountered in existing SMA structures. The stacked structure endures >108 compression cycles and can deliver high specific cooling power of 3850 watts per kilogram. Our S-S method reduces fabrication costs by one order of magnitude compared with existing approaches, enabling mass production of eC refrigerant structures for commercial deployment.

items.title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago.
items.abstract: Cannabis is the world's most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

items.title: The science of the individual.
items.abstract: A new paradigm for behavior change is tested.

items.title: Intravenous Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke - New Directions.
items.abstract: In the past 5 years, substantial changes have been made in the use of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Integrating IVT with endovascular thrombectomy, which improves outcomes in patients with stroke due to large cerebral vessel occlusion, has been a particular challenge. This review discusses the underlying vascular targets for IVT and thrombectomy, the increasing use of tenecteplase instead of alteplase, broadening indications for the use of IVT, and ancillary drugs and dosing methods that may augment the success of IVT.

items.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.

sections.objective: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis.
sections.methods: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing.
sections.results: At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

items.title: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy.

sections.objective: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL.
sections.methods: In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria.
sections.results: A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups.
sections.conclusion: Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

items.title: Retatrutide, a Triple Hormone Receptor Agonist, for Treatment of Obesity.

sections.objective: Retatrutide is a triple-receptor agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, and glucagon receptors.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, randomized, double-blind trial, we assigned adults with obesity without diabetes to receive a once-weekly subcutaneous injection of retatrutide (at a dose of 4 mg, 9 mg, or 12 mg) or placebo for 80 weeks. Primary outcomes (evaluated in the 9-mg and 12-mg groups each vs. placebo) were the percent change in body weight and the change in the WOMAC pain score (ranging from 1 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) in the subgroup of 574 participants with knee osteoarthritis and the change in the apnea-hypopnea index in the 243 participants with obstructive sleep apnea. For weight-related end points, intercurrent events were handled by a treatment-regimen estimand (intention-to-treat [ITT]). For end points in participants with knee osteoarthritis or obstructive sleep apnea, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure; ITT results are also reported.
sections.results: A total of 2339 participants underwent randomization. The mean percent change in body weight in the retatrutide groups was -17.6% (4-mg dose), -23.7% (9-mg dose), and -25.0% (12-mg dose) versus -3.9% in the placebo group (differences, -19.8 and -21.0 percentage points, respectively; P<0.001 for both comparisons). Among the participants with knee osteoarthritis, the corresponding changes in the pain score in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid estimand were -3.2, -3.5, and -3.6 versus -1.9 with placebo (differences, -1.6 and -1.8 points; both P<0.001); the corresponding changes for the ITT estimand were -3.4, -3.9, and -4.1 versus -2.5 with placebo (differences, -1.4 and -1.6 points; both P<0.001). Among the participants with obstructive sleep apnea, the corresponding changes in events per hour in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid-treatment estimand were -22.9, -34.3, and -31.7 versus -9.9 (differences, -24.4 and -21.9; both P<0.001); the corresponding changes for the ITT estimand were -22.8, -34.3, and -32.1 versus -9.6 (differences, -24.7 and -22.5; both P<0.001). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.
sections.conclusion: In adults with obesity, retatrutide resulted in significant weight reduction, reduced pain in participants with knee osteoarthritis, and reduced apnea-hypopnea events in participants with obstructive sleep apnea. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05929066.).

items.title: Targeted Use of Computed Tomographic Coronary Angiography in Acute Chest Pain.

sections.objective: Many patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome in whom myocardial infarction has been ruled out in the emergency department remain at risk for cardiovascular events. Whether further investigation reduces this risk is unknown.
sections.methods: In a multicenter, randomized, controlled trial, patients who presented to an emergency department in 14 hospitals across the United Kingdom were enrolled if myocardial infarction had been ruled out and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin testing indicated an intermediate risk of a cardiovascular event (maximum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I or T concentration, >5 ng per liter). Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either outpatient computed tomographic (CT) coronary angiography-guided care or standard care. The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction or death from a cardiac cause.
sections.results: From September 18, 2019, to May 11, 2023, a total of 3170 participants (median age, 61 years; female sex, 30.2%) were assigned to undergo CT coronary angiography (1587 participants) or receive standard care (1583 participants). At 90 days after randomization, CT coronary angiography had been performed in 1462 participants (92.1%) in the CT coronary angiography group and in 35 participants (2.2%) in the standard-care group. Overall, 7 participants (0.4%) had a CT coronary angiography-related adverse event. After a median of 3.0 years, at which point the number of primary-outcome events in the standard-care group exceeded the prespecified minimum of 97, a primary-outcome event had occurred in 112 participants (7.1%) in the CT coronary angiography group and in 116 (7.3%) in the standard-care group (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% confidence interval, 0.73 to 1.23; P = 0.71).
sections.conclusion: In patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome in whom myocardial infarction had been ruled out, routine CT coronary angiography-guided management did not result in a lower incidence of subsequent myocardial infarction or death from a cardiac cause than standard care. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation; TARGET-CTCA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03952351.).

items.title: Prevalence of Silent Atherosclerosis across Adult Life.

sections.objective: Atherosclerosis may begin in early adulthood and remain clinically silent for decades before cardiovascular disease manifests. Although silent atherosclerosis is associated with cardiovascular events and death independent of traditional cardiovascular disease risk factors, its age- and sex-specific prevalence, vascular territory distribution, and plaque volume across adult life remain incompletely defined.
sections.methods: We conducted a prospective cohort study in Denmark and Spain. Adults 18 to 70 years of age without known atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled in five prespecified age strata that included balanced numbers of women and men. Silent atherosclerosis was assessed at baseline with three-dimensional vascular ultrasonography of the carotid and femoral arteries and with coronary computed tomographic angiography.
sections.results: A total of 16,808 adults were enrolled in the study. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 45±12 years, and 51.4% were women. Silent atherosclerosis was present in 57.1% of the participants (95% confidence interval, 56.3 to 58.0). In the youngest age stratum (18 to 29 years), atherosclerosis was present in 8.7% of the men and 6.7% of the women; prevalence increased with age, with a later, steeper midlife rise among women. Among participants in the younger age strata, atherosclerosis was most often peripheral and confined to a single vascular territory; with increasing age, plaque volume increased exponentially and the prevalence of multiarterial involvement became more frequent. Isolated coronary-artery atherosclerosis was uncommon in every age stratum (≤9.3% of men and ≤5.0% of women).
sections.conclusion: This study of silent atherosclerosis showed that the disease was detectable in early adulthood, with age- and sex-associated increases in prevalence across arterial territories and marked increases in plaque volume. (Funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation; REACT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06692127.).

items.title: Passive Sealing Stent-Grafts for Chimney Endovascular Repair: In Vitro Examination and a Japanese Single-Centre Retrospective Study.

sections.objective: Juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms (JAAAs) present with a short infrarenal neck that does not permit standard endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). The AFX VELA cuff extension with its endoskeletal architecture may reduce type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) through passive sealing. We examined this hypothesis using a double-chimney benchtop model and a clinical cohort treated with VELA-based chimney EVAR (ChEVAR).
sections.methods: A benchtop model compared gutter leakage volumes among VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3 (5 trials per device). A retrospective single-centre cohort (January 2018-April 2024) included consecutive JAAA patients undergoing VELA-based ChEVAR with ≥12-month follow-up. Postoperative computed tomographic (CT) morphometry compared seal-zone geometry across the 3 platforms.
sections.results: In the benchtop model, VELA showed a median gutter leakage of 5.0 mL/min (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-11.0), whereas both comparators exceeded 500 mL/min and were right-censored. In the clinical cohort, 20 patients (55% male; median age 80.0 years) underwent ChEVAR for JAAAs with a median diameter of 53.5 mm and infrarenal neck length of 5.0 mm. Clinically successful sac exclusion was achieved in 19 of 20 patients (95%). Intraoperative TIaEL occurred in 5 patients: 1 major endoleak was sealed with adjunctive gutter coil embolisation, and 4 minor endoleaks resolved spontaneously on the 1-month CT angiogram. Over a median follow-up of 36.5 months, no persistent TIaEL was detected on follow-up imaging, and no chimney stent-graft (SG) occlusion occurred. One patient (5%) required an aortic-related reintervention for a type Ib endoleak. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decreased by ≥20% in 9 patients (45%), and 1 started dialysis at 4 years. On postoperative CT morphometry, relative gutter area was lowest with VELA, intermediate with Endurant II and highest with Excluder C3; circumferential apposition followed the inverse pattern.
sections.conclusion: In the benchtop model, VELA produced consistently lower leakage than both comparators, with concordant CT morphometric evidence consistent with a passive sealing mechanism. In this cohort, VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%) with no persistent TIaEL and no chimney SG occlusion. These findings support the feasibility of VELA-based ChEVAR when FEVAR is unavailable; multicentre prospective validation is required.
sections.other: Persistent type Ia endoleak (TIaEL) is a principal limitation of chimney EVAR (ChEVAR) compared with fenestrated EVAR (FEVAR). We report short-to mid-term outcomes of ChEVAR using the AFX VELA cuff extension, whose endoskeletal architecture is designed to promote passive sealing. Postoperative CT morphometry comparing the 3 devices (VELA, Endurant II and Excluder C3) showed a smaller relative gutter area and higher circumferential apposition with VELA, paralleling the benchtop pattern. VELA-based ChEVAR achieved clinically successful sac exclusion in 19 of 20 patients (95%), without persistent TIaEL detected on follow-up imaging. VELA-based ChEVAR appears feasible when FEVAR is unavailable; however, multicentre validation is required.

items.title: Technical Feasibility and Outcomes of t-Branch Proximal Shortening in Urgent Complex Aortic Repair.

sections.objective: Branched endovascular repair has shown consistently good outcomes, being sometimes the only available endovascular solution for aortic emergencies. However, in cases of limited proximal extension of the disease, such as juxtarenal or pararenal aneurysms, branched endografts usually cover a greater extent of the aorta than needed to establish a seal zone, thus increasing the risk for spinal cord ischemia (SCI) by unnecessarily covering segmental arteries.Our objective is to analyze a series of patients who underwent proximal shortening of an off-the-shelf (OTS) branched endograft to limit aortic coverage and preserve segmental arteries.
sections.methods: Single-center retrospective study identifying all patients undergoing branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) with a shortened t-Branch, through the removal of the first stent row, from April 2020 to March 2026.Perioperative technical success and complications were evaluated. Primary endpoints were technical success. Secondary endpoints were 30-day mortality, SCI, assessment of number of saved segmental arteries, and endograft migration at follow-up.
sections.results: Fifteen patients underwent BEVAR with a shortened t-Branch endograft. All were urgencies, 60% being ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs). Thirteen (86%) cases were juxta/pararenal aortic aneurysms, and 3 (20%) had a previous endovascular aortic repair. In all cases, the proximal sealing stent of the t-Branch was removed, whereas in 2 cases, an additional large posterior fenestration at the second sealing stent was created. Technical success was 93%, with 1 severely stenotic renal artery not able to be catheterized and left unbridged. No endograft deployment complication (migration or malrotation) were experienced. There was 1 postoperative mortality in a patient with a ruptured AAA. Major complication rate was 27%, including 2 patients having SCI (one grade 2, one grade 3). A median of 2 segmental arteries were saved through the endograft modification.At a median follow-up of 1 year no endograft migration was observed.
sections.conclusion: In urgent complex aortic repair for circumscribed anatomies such as juxta/pararenal aneurysms, the use of a modified OTS branched endograft proved to be a reproducible and safe technique, allowing the preservation of segmental arteries and possibly affecting favorably the spinal cord ischemic rates.Clinical ImpactOn-table shortening of the t-Branch endograft, optionally creating a big fenestration at the second sealing stent, is a feasible and reproducible option for urgent juxta/pararenal aortic aneurysm repair when custom-made devices are not available. The modification allowed sparing a median of two segmental arteries otherwise covered with a standard t-Branch, which might help mitigating the risk of spinal cord ischemia.

items.title: Vascular surgeons have better limb salvage outcomes than non-vascular surgeons in chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
items.abstract: BackgroundWhile the treatment of peripheral artery disease with lower extremity bypass is performed primarily by board-certified vascular surgeons, a subset of non-vascular surgeons continues performing these cases. We investigated differences in practice patterns and surgical outcomes between vascular and non-vascular surgeons for bypass in patients with claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI).MethodsThe ACS-NSQIP targeted database from 2011 to 2022 was used to select non-emergent claudication and CLTI patients. Propensity matching (3:1) was applied to balance demographics and comorbidities between vascular and non-vascular surgeons. Claudication and CLTI cohorts were analyzed separately. Thirty-day outcomes were examined.ResultsFemoropopliteal bypass was the most common procedure followed by femoral-distal bypass for both vascular and non-vascular surgeons. Vascular surgeons were more likely to perform femoral-distal procedures and use single-segment saphenous vein grafts (SSSV) for both claudication and CLTI. Vascular surgeons were less likely to use other non-SSSV conduits for claudication patients (40.6% vs 54.6%, p < 0.01), but no difference in CLTI (38.9%% vs 40.1%, p = 0.74). There was no significant difference in 30-day mortality/morbidities between surgeons for either claudication or CLTI. However, 30-day major amputation for CLTI was significantly better with vascular surgeons (3.0% vs 7.5%, p < 0.01). In CLTI patients, after correcting for operation type and conduit usage, vascular surgeons continued to be associated with lower major amputation (aOR = 0.46, 95 CI = 0.29-0.72, p < 0.01).ConclusionVascular surgeons have better limb salvage than non-vascular surgeons. This could not be explained by the higher use of SSSV; thus, other factors such as surgical skill may account for better outcomes.

items.title: The Impact of Undernutrition on Post-Tuberculosis Lung-Function: A Prospective Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Undernutrition is the leading driver of tuberculosis worldwide, yet its effect on the lungs of people who complete treatment is not well defined.
sections.methods: Adults (≥18 years) with drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis were enrolled at treatment initiation in India. We measured associations of baseline body mass index (BMI), mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), and premorbid BMI with spirometry, chest radiograph score, six-minute walk distance and St George's Respiratory Questionnaire score. Plasma IFN-γ, TNF-α and IL-6 were measured at baseline and month 2; counterfactual mediation analysis partitioned the effect of undernutrition on lung function into direct and inflammation-mediated components.
sections.results: Of 156 participants analyzed, 76 (48.7%) had a ventilatory defect; 52 (33.3%) had airflow obstruction and 31 (19.9%) had restrictive spirometry. Each 1 kg/m2 higher baseline BMI was associated with lower odds of any ventilatory defect (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.78; 95% CI, 0.67-0.90), and BMI below 16 kg/m2 carried five-fold higher odds than BMI ≥18.5 kg/m2 (aOR, 5.08; 95% CI, 1.76-16.02). MUAC and premorbid BMI showed similar associations. Lower BMI was associated with restrictive spirometry (aOR, 0.74 per kg/m2; 95% CI, 0.59-0.89) but not airflow obstruction (aOR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.80-1.03). Undernourished participants had higher baseline IL-6, which mediated 32% (FEV1) and 49% (FVC) of the association with impaired lung function.
sections.conclusion: Undernutrition before and at treatment initiation is a potentially modifiable determinant of post-treatment lung impairment, with systemic inflammation mediating part of the effect. Nutritional assessment belongs in routine tuberculosis care, and nutritional support should be tested to prevent lung-function impairment in tuberculosis survivors.
sections.other: Among adults treated for drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis, is undernutrition associated with worse post-treatment lung function, radiographic severity, exercise capacity and respiratory quality of life, and does systemic inflammation mediate that association?

items.title: The impact of removing prior authorization for guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medications for COPD: a population-based cohort study.

sections.objective: Most patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) do not receive maintenance inhaled therapies in concordance with evidence-based clinical guidelines. Long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMA), the recommended first-line therapy, is underused, while inhaled corticosteroids (ICS)/long-acting beta-agonists (LABA) are often used in discordance with clinical guidelines. In July 2020, British Columbia's (BC) universal drug plan removed prior authorization requirements for coverage for LAMA medications and restricted coverage for ICS/LABA.
sections.methods: In a population-based cohort study using provincial administrative health data, we identified patients with COPD using a validated case definition and followed them from January 2019 (18 months pre-policy) to December 2022 (30 months post-policy). Using interrupted time series analysis, we evaluated the monthly proportion of patients filling a prescription for ICS/LABA and LAMA, mean canisters dispensed, proportion of days covered (PDC), rates of ICS/LABA discontinuation, LAMA (re)initiation, and initiating LAMA as first maintenance therapy. We report absolute differences between observed and counterfactual outcomes at study end.
sections.results: The cohort included 47,583 patients with COPD (mean 71.5 years, 46.5% female, 31.7 months mean follow-up). Thirty months post-policy change, ICS/LABA use decreased by -1.3% (95% CI -2.4, -0.3) and LAMA use increased by 0.8% (95% CI 0.1, 1.6). There was no significant change in the number of ICS/LABA canisters dispensed, PDC or proportion discontinuing ICS/LABA. Mean LAMA canisters dispensed increased by 9.8 per 1,000 patients (95% CI 1.0, 18.7) and PDC increased by 1.5% (95% CI 0.5, 2.4). (Re)initiation of LAMA or initiating LAMA as maintenance therapy increased by 0.2% (95% CI 0.02, 0.3) and 34.8% (95% CI 22.3, 48.6), respectively. Total combined drug costs did not change.
sections.conclusion: Changes to drug coverage in BC were associated with improved guideline-concordant medication use.
sections.other: What is the impact of this policy change on guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medication use?

items.title: Pretransplant Pulmonary Hemodynamics, Explant Histology, and Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation for Silicosis.

sections.objective: Silicosis associated with progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is a major cause of end-stage lung disease among workers in the artificial stone industry. Patients with PMF are increasingly referred for lung transplant (LTx) evaluation and there is emerging evidence of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in patients with advanced PMF.
sections.methods: Retrospective single-center cohort study of prospectively-enrolled participants, providing granular data on the invasive hemodynamic profile of patients with silicosis-associated PMF, histopathologic data on pulmonary vascular aberrations, and clinical data on post-transplant complications. Clinical and sociodemographic variables were collected. Explanted lungs from patients with silicosis-associated PMF underwent detailed pulmonary vascular histopathologic review and were descriptively compared with PAH explants. The incidence of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) was evaluated and descriptive analysis performed to provide associations of clinical features and PGD incidence.
sections.results: PH was present in over 95% of 21 patients with silicosis-associated PMF who underwent LTx, with a hemodynamic profile similar to patients transplanted for PAH. . Silicosis explants showed confluent silicotic nodules, extensive fibrosis and hyalinization, obscuration or obliteration of vascular structures, and perivascular fibrohistiocytic infiltrates with extrinsic narrowing. Classic PAH-type arteriolar muscular hypertrophy and plexiform arteriopathy were uncommon. In exploratory comparisons, patients who developed PGD had more frequent pretransplant right ventricular dysfunction (71% vs 21%; risk difference 0.50, 95% CI 0.06-0.75) and a lower median TAPSE/RVSP ratio (0.27 vs 0.39; Hedges' g -0.93, 95% CI -1.88 to 0.02) than in those without PGD.
sections.conclusion: These findings suggest that PH in advanced silicosis with PMF is very common and represents a distinct pulmonary vascular phenotype characterized by extensive fibrotic vascular obliteration rather than the classic arteriopathy seen in PAH.
sections.other: Among patients with PMF referred for lung transplantation, what is the incidence of PH and what are accompanying histopathologic pulmonary vascular aberrations?

items.title: Fluid fluctuation and visual outcomes in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Fluctuation in retinal thickness and fluid during anti-vascular endothelial growrh factor (VEGF) therapy has emerged as a candidate prognostic biomarker in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), but the evidence is heterogeneous and has not been quantitatively synthesized. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to December, 2025, for studies reporting retinal fluid or thickness fluctuation metrics and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) outcomes in eyes receiving anti-VEGF therapy for nAMD, including both observational studies and post hoc analyses of randomized trials. Between-group mean differences (MDs) in BCVA change were pooled using random-effects models, stratified by study design and OCT parameter, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Seventeen studies comprising 19 reports and 9,873 eyes were included. Among observational studies at 24 months, eyes in the highest fluctuation category had significantly smaller BCVA gains than those in the lowest for every parameter examined: intraretinal fluid (MD -7.00 letters, 95% CI -10.27 to -3.72), subretinal fluid (-5.02, -8.09 to -1.95), pigment epithelial detachment (-8.41, -14.54 to -2.27), total fluid (-9.42, -12.69 to -6.15), and central subfield thickness (-10.56, -14.40 to -6.73), with low to moderate heterogeneity (I² 0-42.6%). Among post hoc analyses of randomized trials at 24 months, the pooled difference was -6.02 letters (-8.72 to -3.32), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 77.2%) that leave-one-out analysis showed did not alter the direction or significance of the estimate. Greater fluctuation was additionally associated with approximately twice the odds of macular fibrosis and atrophy. Certainty of evidence was low to very low for most fluid compartments, limited principally by the non-randomized nature of the exposure and by the absence of a standardized definition of fluctuation across studies. Temporal anatomical stability, rather than the presence of fluid at any single visit, may therefore carry prognostic information beyond conventional measures of disease activity, though prospective evaluation using a common metric is required before stability can be adopted as a treatment target.

items.title: Rethinking the timing of congenital ptosis repair: A narrative review.
items.abstract: The optimal timing of congenital ptosis repair remains uncertain when visual development is not immediately threatened. We review the available evidence to distinguish indications for prompt surgery, earlier elective repair, and active surveillance. Visual-axis obstruction or documented or progressive deprivation amblyopia warrants surgery once the child is medically suitable for anesthesia, with intervention within the first 6 months serving as a reasonable pragmatic target. Without an immediate visual threat, earlier elective repair may be considered for significant superior visual-field restriction, documented binocular dysfunction, compensatory chin elevation, functional limitations, or psychosocial concerns. Refractive abnormalities should be treated directly and monitored rather than used alone to determine surgical timing. Laterality, ocular-surface status, procedure suitability, postoperative monitoring, and anesthetic exposure may modify timing. Observation is appropriate for mild, asymptomatic ptosis with normal visual development and reliable follow-up. Direct age-comparative evidence remains sparse and confounded and does not support routine deferral until school age. Clinicians should individualize timing through shared decision-making and reassess it as the child's visual, functional, psychosocial, and surgical circumstances evolve.

items.title: Fetal hemoglobin and sickle cell retinopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Sickle cell retinopathy (SCR) is a vision-threatening complication of sickle cell disease, but the association between fetal hemoglobin (HbF) and SCR has not been quantitatively synthesized. This registered systematic review and meta-analysis (CRD420261486321) evaluated HbF in relation to SCR, particularly proliferative sickle cell retinopathy (PSCR). MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched through June 4, 2026. Studies evaluating HbF in relation to SCR presence, development, or progression were included. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E and certainty using GRADE. Random-effects models pooled adjusted odds ratios (ORs), mean differences, and threshold associations. Eighteen studies were included; 11 contributed to quantitative synthesis. Each 1-percentage-point increase in HbF was associated with lower adjusted odds of PSCR (OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.83-0.92; P<0.001; I²=5.8%) and any SCR (OR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.90-0.95; P<0.001; I²=0%). Higher HbF was also associated with lower adjusted odds of PSCR development or progression (OR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.85-0.94; P<0.001; I²=0%). Mean HbF was lower among patients with SCR, but the pooled difference was not significant (mean difference, -1.30 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.74 to 0.14; P=0.08; I²=73.7%). HbF below 15% was associated with higher odds of SCR (OR, 2.72; 95% CI, 1.64-4.52; P<0.001; I²=0%). Higher HbF was associated with lower odds of SCR, particularly PSCR. Evidence for continuous associations with PSCR and any SCR was of moderate certainty; certainty was lower for secondary analyses. HbF may be an informative marker of retinopathy risk, but current evidence does not establish a target or actionable cutoff.

items.title: Endophthalmitis risk after intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injection using prefilled versus vial-drawn syringes: An agent-specific systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Post-injection endophthalmitis is a rare, vision-threatening complication of intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy. Prefilled syringes may reduce contamination by eliminating point-of-care drug transfer, but prior pooled comparisons may be confounded by anti-VEGF agent, drug mix, and calendar era. We systematically reviewed anti-VEGF studies comparing prefilled with vial-drawn syringes (PROSPERO CRD420251090070). Fourteen comparative studies included 6.2 million injections; nine vial-only cohorts informed the temporal anchoring analysis. Using arm-based generalized linear mixed models, prefilled syringes were associated with lower endophthalmitis odds: the agent-matched odds ratio was 0.62 (95% CI 0.49-0.77) and the all-agent estimate 0.53 (0.43-0.65). Effects were concordant for ranibizumab (0.61) and aflibercept (0.58), with no significant between-agent difference, and culture-positive endophthalmitis was likewise lower with prefilled syringes (OR 0.33). The agent-matched absolute risk difference was approximately 1 fewer case per 10,000 injections. Findings were robust to small-study adjustment and persisted after linear calendar-year adjustment (OR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.53-0.69), with no evidence of a linear year association (P=.93). Prefilled-syringe delivery is associated with approximately one-third lower odds of endophthalmitis than vials-consistent across agents, robust to bias adjustment, and calendar-years adjustments-while acknowledging the residual-confounding limits inherent to observational data.

items.title: Three-Year Outcomes of Trabeculotomy vs Combined Trabeculotomy-Trabeculectomy for Primary Congenital Glaucoma.

sections.objective: To determine whether trabeculotomy is noninferior to combined trabeculotomy-trabeculectomy (CTT) for primary congenital glaucoma (PCG) with a horizontal corneal diameter (HCD) of 12-14 mm.
sections.methods: Prospective, randomized, controlled noninferiority trial. Children from birth through 3 years of age with PCG, a HCD of 12 to 14 mm, and no previous intraocular or laser surgery were eligible. Two hundred and forty-eight children were enrolled from January 2015 through April 2021, and the final follow-up was completed in April 2024. One eligible eye per child was randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to trabeculotomy or CTT.
sections.results: Overall, 124 children were assigned to trabeculotomy (mean age, 9.8 months; 76.6% male) and 124 to CTT (mean age, 9.9 months; 68.5% male). In the intention-to-treat population, qualified success at 36 months was achieved in 102 of 124 eyes (82.3%) in the trabeculotomy group and 105 of 124 eyes (84.7%) in the CTT group (risk difference: -2.4%; 95%CI, -11.7 to 6.9; Pnoninferiority= 0.004). Corresponding rates in the per-protocol population were 90.3% and 92.9%, respectively (risk difference -2.6%; 95%CI -10.3 to 4.9; Pnoninferiority< 0.001). Mean IOP reduction was -12.1 mm Hg (95%CI, -12.9 to -11.4) and -13.2 mm Hg (95%CI, -14.0 to -12.4) in the trabeculotomy and CTT groups, respectively (P=0.067). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in other secondary outcomes. Adverse events occurred in 56 children (45.2%) in the trabeculotomy group and 67 (54.0%) in the CTT group (P = 0.162). Hyphema was the most common adverse event in both groups, and most cases resolved spontaneously.
sections.conclusion: Trabeculotomy was noninferior to CTT for qualified surgical success at 36 months in PCG patients with a HCD of 12-14 mm. These findings suggest that trabeculotomy may be an alternative to CTT in this population.
sections.other: The primary outcome was qualified surgical success at 36 months, defined as an intraocular pressure (IOP) of 5 to 21 mmHg with or without glaucoma medications, without vision-threatening complications or additional glaucoma surgery. The noninferiority margin was -15 percentage points. Exploratory secondary outcomes included changes in IOP, ocular morphometric and functional outcomes, and adverse events.

items.title: Systematic overestimation using in silico-driven curation in a population database caused reevaluation of the genetic prevalence of Alport Syndrome.

sections.objective: A landmark study by Gibson and coworkers in 2021 estimated that one in 106 individuals carry a predicted pathogenic COL4A3 or COL4A4 variant, suggesting autosomal dominant Alport syndrome is massively underdiagnosed. However, pathogenicity of all triple-helical Glycine substitutions was inferred using in silico tools, which may overestimate prevalence.
sections.methods: COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 variants were extracted from population database gnomADv4.1.1 (about 800,000 individuals, including UK Biobank) and from a clinical exome cohort of 29,055 patients (Eurofins Biomnis), stratified into a kidney disease group (KIDNEY) of 8663 individuals and 20,392 individuals of a non-kidney control group (NON-KIDNEY). Three curation strategies were compared: a ClinVar-dependent model, an in silico-driven model adapted from Gibson, and an Expert Strategy combining stringent allele frequency thresholds, high-confidence loss-of-function filtering, and with ClinVar validation for missense variants. Estimates were validated against the control group and replicated in the non-UKB Biobank subset.
sections.results: Applied to gnomADv4.1.1, the Gibson methodology yielded one in 221, a 52% reduction from the original one in 106 (gnomADv2). The Expert Strategy estimated one in 283, validated in the NON-KIDNEY group (one in 295; concordance ratio 0.96), whereas Gibson inflated the control rate by 91% (one in 154 vs. one in 295). Glycine substitutions (COL4A3 p.Gly1277Ser odds ratio 0.95; COL4A4 p.Gly999Glu odds ratio 1.01) were misclassified by all in silico tools. Expert Strategy variants were found in one in 44 KIDNEY patients (odds ratio 6.76). Enrichment was unchanged by high-confidence loss-of-function restriction.
sections.conclusion: Autosomal dominant Alport syndrome affects one in 283 individuals, one to two orders of magnitude above classical clinical estimates (one in 5,000 to one in 53,000), confirming underdiagnosis, but substantially lower than the Gibson estimate. These findings argue for downgrading the PM2 rarity criterion in collagenopathies. Systematic COL4A3/COL4A4 screening in chronic kidney disease is justified by a diagnostic yield of one in 44.

items.title: Modified immune cell therapy targets kidney-resident tertiary lymphoid structures and ameliorates murine lupus nephritis.

sections.objective: Modified immune cells (MIC), i.e. mononuclear cells challenged with mitomycin C can induce immunotolerance. MIC treatment has been successful in several animal models of autoimmunity and in clinical trials after solid organ transplantation, but the mechanism for reduced inflammation is not fully understood.
sections.methods: To investigate the efficacy of MIC therapy in lupus nephritis, splenocytes from syngeneic NZB/W F1 (BWF1) donor mice were incubated with mitomycin C, and then into BWF1 recipients at 25 weeks of age. Animals were followed for another five weeks to assess disease progression by histological, flow cytometric, and serological parameters. An in vitro phagocytosis assay was conducted to determine the clearance of MIC from 25 patients with lupus and from matched healthy individuals by autologous macrophages.
sections.results: In BWF1 mice, MIC therapy reduced the clinical burden of lupus nephritis disease progression with lower protein excretion and lower serum creatinine levels in the standard-dose compared to the control group. High-dose MIC therapy during active diseases showed no additional benefit. More than 86% of animals had dense lymphocytic aggregates close to the kidney pelvis. These tertiary lymphoid structures differed between MIC-treated animals and controls, with a loss of organization, loss of separation of B-cell and T-cell areas and disintegration of germinal centers after MIC treatment. In the peripheral blood, MIC-treated animals had higher numbers of CD19+CD5+CD1dhigh regulatory-like B lymphocytes. Although MIC treatment was beneficial, higher dosing offered no additional clinical benefit in mice. Macrophages from the patients with lupus efficiently cleared MIC in vitro, ruling out defective clearance as a limiting factor.
sections.conclusion: Our clinically applicable cell therapy approach has the potential to control lupus nephritis by specifically dampening deleterious autoimmune responses.

items.title: Ontogenically distinct macrophages occupy discrete kidney niches and contribute to monocyte recruitment in experimental crescentic glomerulonephritis.

sections.objective: Crescentic glomerulonephritis (cGN) is characterized by aggressive immune-mediated glomerular injury with prominent macrophage accumulation that correlates with disease severity. However, the distinct contributions of kidney-resident macrophages (KRMs) of different ontogenies remain poorly defined.
sections.methods: To explore this, we used single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), reporter-based bone marrow chimeras, timed clodronate liposome treatment, and chemokine blockade to define the spatiotemporal dynamics and functional roles of macrophage populations in nephrotoxic serum nephritis (NTSN), a model of cGN.
sections.results: ScRNA-seq of total kidney and CD45+ immune cells revealed that proliferating macrophages and infiltrating monocytes expanded sharply by day five and declined by day ten, indicating that local proliferation, in addition to monocyte recruitment, contributes substantially to early macrophage accumulation in NTSN. Two major KRM subpopulations were distinguished by high Ccr2 or Mrc1 expression, consistent with bone marrow and embryonically seeded, self-renewing KRM population, respectively. In Cx3cr1-GFP recipient mice reconstituted with Ccr2-RFP+ donor bone marrow, embryonic-derived GFP+ KRMs were enriched in the outer medulla and corticomedullary region, whereas donor-derived RFP+ monocytes/macrophages preferentially accumulated in the cortex, including within and around the inflamed glomeruli. A timed clodronate liposome regimen that preferentially reduced recipient-retained GFP+ KRMs decreased the cortical accumulation of RFP+ cells, albuminuria, and histologic kidney injury in NTSN mice. Cell-cell communication analysis identified macrophage-associated CCL12 expression, a murine ortholog of human CCL2, as a candidate mediator of cortical CCR2+ monocyte recruitment. CCL12 neutralization reduced cortical monocyte accumulation and ameliorated kidney damage in NTSN mice.
sections.conclusion: These findings indicate that ontogenically distinct and spatially segregated macrophage populations cooperate during early cGN and support further investigation of the CCR2 axis as a therapeutic target for macrophage-mediated kidney injury in cGN.

items.title: Advances in assessing donor organ quality and perioperative risk for kidney transplantation.
items.abstract: Kidney transplantation faces persistent challenges in accurately evaluating donor organ quality and predicting long-term outcomes, with traditional assessment methods demonstrating limited predictive capacity. The increasing utilization of marginal-quality donor organs has intensified the need for sophisticated evaluation strategies. Machine perfusion technology has transformed organ preservation from mere static storage to a dynamic platform potentially enabling real-time monitoring, assessment, and interventions during the preservation period. Molecular profiling technologies such as genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics could provide refined biomarkers for donor kidney assessment across several phases of kidney transplantation. The first window arises during donor evaluation. Techniques such as high-resolution molecular typing, genetic profiling, epigenomic markers, and artificial intelligence-enhanced imaging provide additional information compared to traditional scoring systems. During organ preservation, a second window emerges, allowing additional, isolated assessment of the organ after procurement but before transplantation. Machine perfusion systems enable sampling of perfusate and tissue for multi-omics analysis to characterize injury or function, although most candidate biomarkers remain at the discovery or early validation stage. After transplantation, donor-derived cell-free deoxyribonucleic acid, urinary chemokines, and advanced imaging modalities offer non-invasive early detection of graft injury. Clinical translation of these new techniques faces substantial challenges: most studies are single-center and have small sample sizes, assay standardization remains incomplete, and evidence linking biomarker-guided decisions to improved long-term graft survival is lacking. Machine learning may enhance risk stratification but remains largely unvalidated in prospective trials. Future progress requires a shift from short-term endpoint prediction to long-term outcome validation through multicenter studies, standardized protocols, and equitable implementation strategies.

items.title: Associations between Antidiabetic Drug Classes and Aortic Aneurysm Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Nationwide Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a potentially life threatening condition that often remains asymptomatic for prolonged periods. Although type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) increases cardiovascular risk, epidemiological studies have paradoxically reported a lower incidence of AA in patients with T2DM. Antidiabetic therapies may contribute to this inverse association, but class specific effects remain unclear. This study evaluated associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA.
sections.methods: This was a nationwide, population based, retrospective cohort study of adults with T2DM in Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database between 2009 and 2022. Associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models with time varying medication exposure, adjusted for demographic characteristics, diabetes severity, comorbidities, tobacco related diagnoses, and concomitant medications. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were considered exploratory.
sections.results: Among 3 295 564 adults with T2DM (mean age 60.0 years; 52.8% men) followed for 8.5 ± 4.7 years, 45.5% received at least three antidiabetic drug classes. In multivariable time varying Cox models, metformin (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.78, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.75 - 0.82), thiazolidinediones (aHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.65 - 0.77), sulfonylureas/meglitinides (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.78 - 0.85), and α-glucosidase inhibitors (aHR 0.83, 95% CI 0.77 - 0.89) were associated with lower AA risk. DPP-4 inhibitors (aHR 0.95, 95% CI 0.90 - 1.00), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors (aHR 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), and glucagon like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) (aHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50 - 0.95) also showed inverse associations, whereas insulin use was associated with higher AA risk (aHR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08 - 1.20). The inverse associations of conventional oral antidiabetic agents remained robust across sensitivity analyses. In contrast, the inverse associations for DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors, and GLP-1RAs were attenuated and no longer statistically significant in patients with an index date from 2011 onward.
sections.conclusion: In this nationwide T2DM cohort, conventional oral antidiabetic agents were consistently associated with a lower observed AA risk. Although newer glucose lowering therapies showed similar inverse associations, these findings were less robust and warrant cautious interpretation and prospective confirmation.

items.title: Baseline Macular OCT Thickness of Ocular Hypertensive Patients Improves Prediction of Glaucoma.

sections.objective: To determine whether baseline macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) and circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (cpRNFL) thickness add prognostic value for glaucomatous visual field (VF) damage in patients with ocular hypertension.
sections.methods: Retrospective clinical cohort study. 330 eyes of 235 patients with ocular hypertension, defined by intraocular pressure of 22 mmHg or higher or an International Classification of Diseases coded diagnosis, without repeatable glaucomatous VF damage at baseline. Eyes came from both the African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study and a clinical cohort at the Shiley Eye Institute. Baseline GCIPL and cpRNFL thickness were measured from the first good-quality Cirrus optical coherence tomography (OCT) macular and optic-disc cubes. Clinical predictors were assessed with the Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study (OHTS)-European Glaucoma Prevention Study (EGPS) Risk Calculator. Repeatable glaucomatous VF damage required a Glaucoma Hemifield Test outside normal limits or a pattern standard deviation at the 5% level or worse on three consecutive reliable Humphrey 24-2 examinations.
sections.results: Glaucomatous VF damage developed in 47 of 330 eyes (14%) over a median 4.4 years. Adjusted for the Risk Calculator, thinner macular GCIPL was associated with conversion (hazard ratio [HR] 1.89 per 1-SD thinner; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.50 to 2.37; P < .001), and every macular sector was significant (HR 1.71 to 2.02). The Risk Calculator alone showed modest discrimination (Harrell C-index, 0.57). Adding macular GCIPL improved discrimination (ΔC +0.101; 95% CI, +0.022 to +0.220). Global cpRNFL thickness did not improve discrimination (ΔC +0.004; 95% CI, -0.021 to +0.133); among cpRNFL quadrants, only the inferior quadrant was associated with conversion (HR 1.50; 95% CI, 1.02 to 2.22).
sections.conclusion: In patients with ocular hypertension, thinner baseline macular GCIPL was associated with glaucomatous VF damage and improved the discrimination of the OHTS-EGPS Risk Calculator, whereas global cpRNFL thickness did not.
sections.other: Hazard ratios per 1 standard deviation (SD) of thinner global and sectoral GCIPL or cpRNFL, and the change in the Harrell concordance (C) index (ΔC) after adding each measure to the Risk Calculator.

items.title: Opposing excitatory and inhibitory synaptic pathologies drive ZC4H2-associated intellectual disability.
items.abstract: Understanding genotype-phenotype correlations is critical for precision medicine, yet patients carrying mutations in the same gene are often classified under one disorder and treated alike, despite potentially opposite responses to therapy. ZC4H2-associated rare disorder (ZARD) is an X-linked neurodevelopmental condition caused by diverse mutations across ZC4H2. Here, we show that distinct ZC4H2 mutations drive intellectual disability through opposing synaptic mechanisms. The gain-of-function mutation ZC4H2L66H enhances GABAA receptor (GABAAR) degradation, impairing inhibitory synaptic transmission and plasticity. By contrast, the loss-of-function mutation ZC4H2R213W increases AMPA receptor (AMPAR) stability and dysregulates excitatory synaptic activity. Despite these diametrically opposed synaptic pathologies, ZC4H2L66H/y and ZC4H2R213W/y knockin mice exhibit comparable cognitive deficits. Importantly, muscimol, a GABAAR agonist, specifically rescues deficits in ZC4H2L66H/y mice, whereas the AMPAR antagonist perampanel rescues ZC4H2R213W/y mice. These findings demonstrate that opposing synaptic etiologies can underlie a single genetic disorder and highlight pathomechanism-based stratification for targeted therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Effect of Electronic Behavioral Nudges on Low-Value Preoperative Testing: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: Robust randomized trials have demonstrated that routine testing before cataract surgery does not improve outcomes; however, despite this evidence and long-standing professional society recommendations discouraging routine testing, preoperative testing remains frequent in real-world practice, with most patients undergoing cataract surgery receiving at least 1 preoperative test. To measure whether electronic health record (EHR)-embedded, behavioral science-informed nudges reduce preoperative testing.
sections.methods: This pragmatic randomized clinical trial was conducted at a large academic health system (UCLA Health) in Los Angeles, California. Physicians performing preoperative evaluations were randomized to 1 of 3 EHR nudge alerts or usual care. All encounters with patients undergoing a preoperative visit with a randomized physician within 30 days of cataract surgery were silently enrolled. Patients were enrolled from June 24, 2021, to April 11, 2023. Data were analyzed from June 2020 (1 year prior to first enrollment) to April 2024 (1 year after last enrollment). The EHR interruptive alerts cited professional society recommendations against routine testing; each emphasized a different potential patient harm, including lack of safety benefit, financial burden, or psychological stress.
sections.results: During the enrollment period, 229 of 776 randomized physicians had 1 or more eligible encounter during which a patient was enrolled. Together, these clinicians had 1045 preoperative encounters during the intervention period with 967 unique patients. Mean (SD) patient age was 72.1 (9.1) years, and 595 encounters (56.9%) were with female patients. Mean (SD) signed preoperative testing rates decreased from 83% (29%) to 79% (31%) in the combined intervention arms vs 84% (30%) to 82% (31%) in the control arm. In mixed-effects models, exposure to any nudge was not associated with a reduction in overall testing (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.68; 95% CI, 0.34-1.34). In prespecified secondary analyses, 16% of orders were cancelled following exposure to a nudge, and the psychological stress nudge was associated with decreases in rates of complete blood cell count (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.75; P = .01) and electrocardiogram orders (aOR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.21-0.83; P = .01) vs control.
sections.conclusion: This randomized clinical trial of EHR nudges did not reach statistical significance on the primary outcome of overall preoperative testing. Secondary outcomes suggest future studies might consider the role of a psychological stress nudge in combination with other behavioral, workflow, and/or payment changes.
sections.other: The primary outcome was the change in the proportion of preoperative cataract surgery encounters with any signed testing order(s) between the 12-month period before the physicians' first encounter (enrollment) and the 12-month postencounter period. Secondary outcomes included order cancellation rates among clinicians exposed to the intervention, separate comparisons of each nudge, and analyses comparing orders for specific categories of tests.

items.title: Potential Disparities in Access to Adult Strabismus Care.

sections.objective: Adult strabismus impacts quality of life through diplopia, eye strain, and psychological burden. Access to care may be limited by various factors, yet disparities in adult strabismus care have not been examined nationally. To evaluate potential disparities in access to adult strabismus care across the US by practice type, insurance status, and county-level socioeconomic characteristics.
sections.methods: This national secret shopper study used standardized telephone calls to US pediatric ophthalmology practices identified through the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus and the American Academy of Ophthalmology that simulated appointment scheduling for an adult patients with strabismus. Of 1064 practices contacted, 1060 were included after excluding 4 clinics with disconnected phone numbers. These data were analyzed from August 2025 to September 2026.
sections.results: Overall, 23.8% (252 of 1060) of practices offered an appointment under at least 1 insurance scenario. Patients using Medicaid had a lower appointment success rate than those with commercial insurance (161 of 648 [24.8%] vs 91 of 194 [46.9%]; difference, -22.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -29.8 to -14.3; P < .001). In multivariable regression, other practice types (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.82; 95% CI, 1.28-2.58; P = .001) and commercial insurance (aOR, 2.36; 95% CI, 1.67-3.33; P = .001) had higher appointment success, while majority racial and ethnic minority counties (aOR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.45-0.97; P = .04) and lower median household income counties (aOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.44-0.93; P = .02) had lower odds. Among practices offering appointments, academic centers had longer wait times than other practices (mean [SD], 95.1 [59.3] days vs 57.0 [54.1] days; 38.1 days difference; 95% CI, 21.2-55.1; P < .001), as did lower-income counties (mean [SD], 78.6 [68.1] days vs 61.3 [52.6] days; -17.4 days difference; 95% CI, -33.3 to -1.4; P = .03).
sections.conclusion: This national secret shopper study identified potential disparities in adult strabismus care access. Commercial insurance and other practice types had higher appointment success, while majority racial and ethnic minority and lower-income counties had reduced access and longer wait times. These findings highlight a potential unmet likely benefit of adult strabismus practitioners and support targeted policy interventions to improve equitable access to care.
sections.other: Practice type (academic vs other), insurance type (Medicaid vs commercial insurance), and county-level characteristics, including race and ethnicity majority, median household income, Area Deprivation Index (ADI), and Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). Appointment success (ability to schedule appointment during call) and appointment wait time (days between call date and earliest available appointment).

items.title: Genome-Wide Association Study Meta-Analysis of Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.

sections.objective: The pathophysiology of central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) remains incompletely understood, and there is ongoing debate regarding the origin of primary dysfunction. To elucidate the genetic architecture of CSC and map susceptibility loci to specific ocular cell types and molecular pathways.
sections.methods: This genetic association study was a genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis aggregating data from 5 large biobank cohorts and included 2584 patients with CSC and 1 044 455 control participants of European ancestry. Cohort data were from July 1, 2010, to October 31, 2023; data analysis was performed from Febuary 2024 to January 2026. Post-GWAS functional mapping was performed using mendelian randomization, bayesian colocalization, and single-cell disease relevance scoring across human ocular tissue atlases. The relevance of the genetic findings was demonstrated by building a CSC genetic risk score and applying it to the UK Biobank (UKB).
sections.results: The meta-analysis identified 10 risk loci reaching the genome-wide threshold (P < 5 × 10-8), including 3 novel loci (TGFB1, LINC00551, and LOC105375630) and 7 replicated loci (CFH, GATA5, PREX1, CD46, NOTCH4, PTPRB, and TNFRSF10A). Integrative post-GWAS analysis prioritized 10 genes, including TGFB1, TNFRSF10A, and CFH, as likely causal effectors. Single-cell enrichment mapping revealed that CSC genetic risk is concentrated in scleral tissue (P < .001) and vascular endothelial cells (P < .001). Mendelian randomization pointed to circulating TGFB1 and TNFRSF10A levels as associated with CSC risk. A CSC genetic risk score applied in UKB revealed a higher frequency of CSC-relevant abnormalities on macular optical coherence tomography in participants in the top 1% of polygenic risk (18/109 [16.5%] vs 8/134 [6.0%]; difference, 10.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 2.6-19.1; adjusted odds ratio, 4.05; 95% CI, 1.65-10.87; P = .002).
sections.conclusion: Convergent genetic evidence supports CSC as a primary disorder of the sclera and choroidal vasculature with retinal pigment epithelium changes likely representing a downstream consequence. Integrative post-GWAS analysis pointed to complement regulation (CFH, CD46), vascular integrity and endothelial cell signaling (PTPRB, TNFRSF10A, NOTCH4, PREX1), and scleral extracellular matrix biology (TGFB1) as important in CSC.
sections.other: Identification of risk loci reaching the genome-wide threshold, prioritized putative causal genes, enrichment of genetic risk within specific ocular tissues and cell types, and performance of a GRS in the independent UKB dataset.

items.title: Electrocardiographic and Echocardiographic Markers of Atrial and Ventricular Remodeling Allow Identification of Cardiac Sarcoidosis.

sections.objective: Cardiac sarcoidosis (CS) is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of systemic sarcoidosis. Although positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging provide high diagnostic accuracy, they are unsuitable for first-line screening. Widely available modalities such as electrocardiography (ECG) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) focusing only on ventricular abnormalities show limited sensitivity. This study aims to evaluate whether a combined diagnostic model integrating ECG and TTE parameters, emphasizing atrial and ventricular remodeling, can accurately identify patients with CS.
sections.methods: We prospectively included 252 consecutive patients with biopsy-proven sarcoidosis. CS was defined by characteristic findings on PET-CT or cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. A comprehensive set of atrial and ventricular ECG and TTE parameters was analyzed. Diagnostic models were constructed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and discriminative performance was assessed.
sections.results: CS was identified in 37 (14.7%) patients. On ECG, prolonged P-wave duration, prolonged QRS duration, and reduced T-wave amplitude in lead aVR were independently associated with CS. On TTE, increased left atrial volume index, increased left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, and impaired left ventricular global longitudinal strain emerged as significant predictors. ECG- and TTE-based models showed comparable discrimination for CS identification (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.87 for both). A combined ECG/TTE model, driven primarily by QRS duration, left atrial volume index, and left ventricular global longitudinal strain, achieved the highest diagnostic performance (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.90).
sections.conclusion: An exploratory multimodal, noninvasive approach integrating atrial and ventricular ECG and TTE markers provides high diagnostic accuracy for identifying CS and may serve as a pragmatic screening and triage tool to guide referral for advanced cardiac imaging. Clinical Trial Registration DRKS00031557 on drks.de (German Clinical Trials Register).

items.title: An information-theoretic framework for inferring T cell dynamics from single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing.
items.abstract: Single-cell T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing enables simultaneous profiling of gene expression and TCR sequences, providing a coregistered measure of T cell phenotypic diversity and clonal dynamics. However, principled probabilistic frameworks for joint modeling of clonotype and phenotype have remained limited.
